thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PRIVATE_VPC_CONNECTIVITY - customer=AcmeCorp env=prod region=eu-west-1 - Group: private-controlplane - Severity: P1

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: incident INC-2026-056; triggered by probe 'private-controlplane-heartbeat' - escalation policy: oncall-sre -> netops -> eng-platform

maya: ACK - I'm on it. Taking primary. @sam I may need net routing help, pinging netops.

sam: On call, stepping in. Any initial indicators? packet loss? route flaps?

maya: From monitoring: control-plane heartbeat missing for customer AcmeCorp 09:12:12 UTC. Agent heartbeat dropped ~09:10. BGP sessions show intermittent drops. TLDR: private control plane not reachable from agent in customer's VPC.

lina: Noted. Is this affecting inference traffic or just telemetry? Any 5xxs reported?

jordan: Customer reports 503s across private deployment endpoints. Confirming support ticket opened by Alex (CS).

alex-cs: Customer says "all inference calls failing for prod cluster, started ~09:10, huge user impact". They've flipped traffic to hosted but want private fixed ASAP.

maya: Steps I'm doing now: 1) fetching agent logs; 2) checking VPC peering/route table; 3) confirming NAT/gateway status. Posting commands I'm running:
```
ssh ops@bastion-eu
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=private-agent --field-selector=status.phase=Running
kubectl -n redwood logs private-agent-acme-01 --tail=200
ssh agent@10.0.4.12 "sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 500"
```

sam: pinged netops. Netops, can you confirm if there were any infra changes or security group updates in eu-west-1 at 09:00-09:15?

netops: We saw a partial BGP convergence event in eu-west-1 at 09:08 due to a router reconfig push to spine-3. That caused transient route withdrawal to some customer subnets. Investigating whether peering to AcmeCorp's VPC was impacted.

jordan: From private-monitoring: control-plane API timed out 09:09-09:18 for AcmeCorp agent IPs. Multiple retries caused client 503s.

maya: Collected logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts from agent to control plane: "handshake timeout after 120s". Agent's network stack shows RSTs. Attaching snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T09:10:07Z private-agent-acme-01 redwood-agent[2321]: WARN connect: tls handshake timeout to cp.redwood.internal:443
2026-03-14T09:10:12Z kernel: IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=... SRC=10.0.4.12 DST=34.89.12.45 PROTO=TCP SPT=52344 DPT=443 RST
```

lina: If it's RSTs from the routing layer, could be due to misapplied firewall or peering ACL. Netops, any ACL changes?

netops: No planned ACL changes. We are rolling back the spine-3 config now to previous good commit and re-advertising routes. ETA ~7m.

maya: Meanwhile mitigation: I'm initiating controlled restart of the private agent on Acme side to see if it re-establishes session post-route fix. Liaising with Acme on-prem contact. Commands I'm proposing (will run after permission):
```
ssh acme-admin@acme-bastion
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'host cp.redwood.internal and port 443' -c 200 -w /tmp/acme-handshake.pcap
```

alex-cs: Acme ops is on the call and gave permission for restart. They asked that we coordinate to avoid simultaneous restarts across their fleet.

pagerduty: Alert update: acknowledged by maya at 09:13:10 UTC. PagerDuty will escalate to netops if not resolved by 09:23:10 UTC.

sam: Good. Maya, please confirm when you restart and paste result logs. I'll keep netops coordination and update the incident channel.

maya: Restarting agent now on acme-host-01. Will wait 30s for connection.

maya: Restart logs: agent restarted, attempting handshake... still failing - TLS timeout persists.

netops: Rollback completed on spine-3 at 09:18:40 UTC. BGP sessions restored. We're seeing route advertisements to AcmeCorp prefixes. Please retry.

maya: Re-checking agent connectivity. Running tcpdump shows SYN then SYN-ACK then RST from an intermediate hop to our control-plane IPs.

jordan: Looks like a middlebox (maybe cloud firewall or customer NVA) is sending RSTs, possibly due to connection tracking exhaustion. Any quota alerts?

lina: Reminder: our runbook suggests temporary fallback to hosted inference for affected customers while deep-dive continues. Alex, confirm customer wants continued failover?

alex-cs: They already shifted some traffic to hosted. They want private fixed but asked us to keep hosted fallback active until all green.

sam: Escalating to eng-platform for on-prem agent protocol checks. @eng-platform can you validate certificate expiry and control-plane listener health?

eng-platform: Jumping in. Certificate for cp.redwood.internal valid until 2027. Control-plane pods in eu-west-1 show healthy CPU/memory; logs show many connection resets on accept side. Suggesting we run a connectivity check from multiple vantage points.

maya: I'm running these checks now from three nodes: 
```
curl -v https://cp.redwood.internal/health -H "Host: cp.redwood.internal" --resolve cp.redwood.internal:443:34.89.12.45
nc -vz cp.redwood.internal 443
traceroute -n cp.redwood.internal
```

maya: Results: Node in eu-west-1 can reach CP IP but TLS handshake fails. Node in us-east can't reach CP IP at all (route not advertised).

netops: US-east routing inconclusive; focused on eu-west where customer is. Netops: confirming intermediate hop (10.10.200.1) is a cloud firewall managed by provider; opening ticket with cloud provider to investigate RSTs.

jordan: Incident severity remains P1 due to customer production impact. Creating incident page: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-056 (runbook link and timeline added).

maya: Quick mitigation idea: If we can temporarily allow agent to use an alternate control-plane IP in same AZ that avoids the firewall path, we could restore connectivity. Eng-platform, can you spin up a spare cp IP in eu-west and BGP-advertise it?

eng-platform: We can allocate a spare CP instance and announce, but that will take ~12m to warm and ensure certs/trust. Alternative: enable our fallback control-plane LB DNS for Acme only and whitelist their IPs - can be faster (~5-8m).

sam: Go with fastest path: eng-platform, enable fallback LB for Acme and inform Maya when done. Netops continue provider ticket. Alex, keep customer updated: hosted fallback remains; working on private restore.

eng-platform: Fallback LB enabled for Acme at 09:34 UTC. Maya, please test agent connectivity to fallback endpoint: cp-fb-eu.redwood.internal

maya: Testing now... agent connects, TLS handshake succeeds to fallback LB. Agent re-registering, heartbeats resumed. 09:36:05 UTC - agent status = READY.

alex-cs: Confirmed from Acme: private endpoints show recovered status for a subset of calls. They're slowly shifting some traffic back.

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: escalation stopped; incident acknowledged. If any re-occur, new alert will be created.

sam: Great. Keeping incident open for follow-up: root cause deep-dive with cloud provider and review of route config changes that caused BGP convergence. Action items:
- [netops] get provider ticket number and RCA (ETA 24h)
- [eng-platform] rotate any certs/add fallback LB hardening (ETA 48h)
- [sre/maya] run postmortem timeline and decide whether to add more control-plane redundancy per-customer (ETA 72h)
- [cs/alex] confirm customer fully recovered and gather impact metrics

maya: I'll hand off to @lina for the rest of the on-call window. Lina - I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and handover cmd history.

lina: Taking over. Thanks @maya. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and coordinate the postmortem.

jordan: Closing notes: created follow-up ticket INT-2026-432 for control-plane redundancy improvements. Will add provider ticket once received.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-056 updated: status=mitigated state=open assignees=[maya, netops, eng-platform] severity=P1

lina: Marking this thread resolved for immediate customer impact. Will reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
